reflections.title: "He Formed It into Another Vessel"

reflect.text: When Jeremiah went down to the potter's shop, he watched clay turn on the wheel. The jar the potter was making became flawed and spoiled in his hands. Yet the craftsman did not throw the ruined lump into the trash. As Adrian Rogers pointed out, God is the Master Workman who takes ordinary, flawed people and reshapes them. Every single turn of the wheel stays completely under His loving control.

Often our own pride or self-will hinders the work God desires to do. When we see our past mistakes, we might fear our lives are ruined. But God does not cast us away. Instead, as F. B. Meyer wrote, He "makes us again." God can take whatever is left of our years and build something truly good. We simply need to yield ourselves to Him, confessing our failures and trusting Him to rebuild us. Just as He restored followers like Peter and Mark in Scripture, He patiently starts over with any heart ready to say yes.

questions: Where have past mistakes made you feel like you are beyond God's use?
How can you yield your life back to the Master Workman today?
reflections.prayer: Lord, thank You that You do not throw me away when I fail. Take my brokenness and reshape my heart according to Your will. Please make me new and help me serve You faithfully. Amen.

reflections.title: "Like Clay in the Potter's Hand"

reflect.text: God compares His people to clay resting in an artisan's hands. He is actively molding our lives, turning plain earth into a vessel of beauty and purpose. Clay must remain soft and pliable so the craftsman can work smoothly. Often, the hard and painful seasons we face are the exact moments when the Potter is shaping us. This transformation is an ongoing daily process that asks us to trust God quietly rather than living in constant worry about the future.

God has a sovereign plan for every life, but we each face a choice. We can either yield to God's molding hands or stiffen our necks against Him. Greg Laurie explains that stubborn resistance leaves a person in danger of spiritual ruin. When we choose to stay soft and pliable, God freely works His guidance into our lives, fashioning us into what He originally designed us to be.

questions: Are there difficult circumstances right now where God might be shaping your character?
In what area of your life are you tempted to resist God's gentle touch?
reflections.prayer: Father, help me remember that I am clay in Your hands. Keep my heart soft and teach me to trust You during painful times. Shape my life according to Your good design. Amen.

reflections.title: Surrendering to the Artisan

reflect.text: Turning raw clay into a masterpiece is careful, demanding work. The artisan must invest deep patience, energy, and vision, making sure the clay is centered firmly before the wheel begins to spin. Through Jeremiah's visit to the potter's house, God reminds us of His sovereign craftsmanship. The Lord sees the end from the beginning, knowing exactly how to refine His people into vessels fit for His glory.

Too often, we try to take over the craftsman's role. Human nature wants to direct God, choosing our own path rather than submitting to His perfect wisdom. Surrendering control means trusting that the Maker knows far better than we do what we need to become. Our only responsibility is to remain centered and pliable under His guidance. When we patiently endure His refining process, God creates a life that honors Him.

questions: In what ways do you try to take control and tell God how your life should go?
What does it look like to remain centered and surrender to God's vision for you this week?
reflections.prayer: Sovereign Lord, forgive me for trying to control my own life and direct Your plans. Help me to rest patiently on Your wheel while You center and refine me. Shape me into a vessel that brings glory to Your name. Amen.
